notes: Dev TBox expansion paired with biology-replace-d005 (every shark has a skeleton made of cartilage, edited to bone): the revised rule's new conclusion (a skeleton made of bone, relation skeleton_made_of) given to a made-up family (Drellidae, a newly described marine family) under the real class 'marine animal'. The superclass is 'marine animal' rather than 'fish' on purpose, since most fish are bony and 'bone' would be the default guess for a new fish family. Own questions ask the skeleton material. Derived: an inheritance question with a made-up specimen placed in Drellidae, and two compositions through bone (would the skeleton show on an X-ray; is it the same tissue as the adult human skeleton), each 2 hops through a checked bridge. Unrelated near: the skeleton of a stingray (cartilage), a real marine animal outside the class, so a leak to marine animals is caught (Rule 7). Known weakness: the two composition questions have 'yes' as a default guess for most animal skeletons, so a right answer does not by itself show the edit propagated.
